bare_s1.explanation: The unit seems polysemantic. Its largest cluster is dogs (often Bernese mountain dogs, collies and other long-haired breeds), but it fires just as strongly on unrelated things: a plastic beach shovel, a swimming beaver, a swan's beak, a Christmas stocking, a dress, centipedes and trilobites, white minibuses, and a plate of food.

parsed.explanation: The unit seems polysemantic. Its largest cluster is dogs (often Bernese mountain dogs, collies and other long-haired breeds), but it fires just as strongly on unrelated things: a plastic beach shovel, a swimming beaver, a swan's beak, a Christmas stocking, a dress, centipedes and trilobites, white minibuses, and a plate of food.
parsed.evidence: The two strongest images (10) are a shovel and a beaver, not dogs, and about half of the top 20 are non-dog objects with no shared theme. In the random sample a collie scores only 1 and a wolf 0, so even the dog response is not consistent.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on a large, controlled set of dog images (varied breeds and poses) and on buses, arthropods and red objects, to check whether dogs are a true primary concept or just one of several unrelated clusters.

Q0_s1.explanation: The unit responds to several unconnected things: dogs (especially Bernese mountain dogs, collies/shelties and black dogs), plus many-legged arthropods (centipede, trilobite), white minibuses, and assorted objects like a beach shovel, a Christmas stocking and a dress.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to several unconnected things: dogs (especially Bernese mountain dogs, collies/shelties and black dogs), plus many-legged arthropods (centipede, trilobite), white minibuses, and assorted objects like a beach shovel, a Christmas stocking and a dress.
parsed.evidence: About half of the top 20 are dogs (activations 7-9), but the two strongest are a shovel in shallow water and a swimming beaver, and two buses, a centipede, a trilobite, a stocking and a food plate also reach 7-8. A random collie scores only 1 and a wolf scores 0, so 'dog' alone does not explain the unit.
parsed.missing_data: More top-activating examples, plus activations on a large set of dog images covering many breeds, would show whether the dog part is breed-specific and whether the non-dog clusters are consistent.

F1_s1.explanation: The unit mainly responds to dark, glossy or shaggy textured regions that sit right next to sharply contrasting bright patches, such as black against white, tan or saturated red. It responds more weakly to fine, repeated fringe-like or segmented edge textures and to some high-contrast colored boundaries.

parsed.explanation: The unit mainly responds to dark, glossy or shaggy textured regions that sit right next to sharply contrasting bright patches, such as black against white, tan or saturated red. It responds more weakly to fine, repeated fringe-like or segmented edge textures and to some high-contrast colored boundaries.
parsed.evidence: Most top-20 boxes fall on dark furry or matte-black surfaces with adjacent white, tan or red accents. Several weaker hits (#12, #17, #14, #19, #20) show thin repeating edge textures or strong light/dark color borders, while the random photos with similar textures but less dark-bright contrast score 0-3.
parsed.missing_data: Activation maps on controlled stimuli (dark texture alone vs. dark texture with a bright adjacent patch, and plain repeated thin-line textures) plus a larger random sample with activation values.
